\begin{proof}
Let $g:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $g(x)=f(x)-x$. Since $f$ is continuous, $g$ is continuous. If $f(0)=0$ or $f(1)=1$, there is already a fixed point. Otherwise, $f(0)\ne0$ and $f(1)\ne1$. As $f(0),f(1)\in[0,1]$, this implies $f(0)>0$ and $f(1)<1$. Consequently,
\[
g(0)=f(0)>0,\qquad g(1)=f(1)-1<0.
\]
By the intermediate value theorem, $g$ vanishes at some $x\in(0,1)$. Therefore $f(x)=x$.
\end{proof}
